title: reconcilePass keys the 'stuck' age on applied_at (signup time) which the claim CAS never stamps and income-signup never writes — so the FIND-003 operator path both MISSES genuinely-stuck rows and FALSE-FLAGS fresh in-flight rows; the unit test never exercises the live applied_at->ts mapping.
description: reconcileStuck (bank-payout-watcher.mjs:70-78) flags a 'processing' row when now - Date.parse(row.ts) >= olderThanMs. The live reconcilePass (line 157-168) supplies ts from r.applied_at (SELECT id,applied_at, line 161-163). But applied_at is the SIGNUP timestamp, never a claim/processing timestamp: (a) the claim CAS uses buildClaimPatch() = {status:'processing'} (line 36) and stamps NO timestamp; (b) income-signup.js inserts only {email,reason,notes,status} (income-signup.js:65-70) and never sets applied_at, and bank-recipients ordering uses 'applied_at.asc.nullslast' (line 110) implying applied_at is routinely NULL. Two defects follow: DEFECT-A (dead operator path): for the common NULL-applied_at row, Date.parse(null/undefined)=NaN -> Number.isFinite(NaN) is false -> the row is NEVER flagged, so a truly stuck 'processing' row (FIND-003's whole reason for existing) is never surfaced to 'needs_review'. DEFECT-B (false flag of in-flight rows): a row claimed seconds ago whose applied_at (signup) is older than the threshold is flagged 'needs_review' WHILE its bank transfer is still in flight, pulling it out of the normal processing->submitted->paid progression prematurely. (No double-pay results because no watcher reads 'needs_review', so this is high not critical — but it defeats the operator-recovery requirement and can mis-route healthy money in flight.) The unit test (bank-payout-watcher.test.js:72-86) injects rows already shaped as {id, ts:<ISO>} directly into reconcileStuck and therefore NEVER exercises the live applied_at->ts mapping, so it stays green while the live reconcilePass is broken — a coverage gap masking a real defect.
recommendation: Stamp a claim/processing timestamp atomically with the CAS: buildClaimPatch() should set { status:'processing', processing_at: new Date().toISOString() } (and add the column), then reconcilePass must SELECT and key on processing_at (NOT applied_at). Add a test that feeds reconcilePass a live-shaped row {id, processing_at:<old>} AND a NULL-timestamp row, asserting the old one is flagged and the NULL one is handled by an explicit policy (flag-after-grace or alert), not silently dropped.
